conviction_note: A small long lean. The EPS bar was cut about 15% in two weeks, from $15.39 (Sep 28) to $12.86-13.02 (Oct 12), with 17 downward revisions and none up, and the LSEG equities consensus of $4.68bn sits below Q2's $3.26bn equities-financing run-rate plus any plausible intermediation. Against that, FICC looks soft, the IB-fee proxy runs slightly under consensus, and this name has sold two of its last four beats. So p_up is 56 on an abs move of 4.5, giving +0.54. That sits a little under the +0.9 impact_sum because the scaled number also carries the macro (10y +87bp in Q3, Fed hike) and the same-morning JPM/C/WFC prints, which can swamp a single-name beat.
bar: EPS ~$12.86-13.02 and revenue ~$16.71-16.87bn, from three agreeing sources dated Oct 12: LSEG via IG ($13.02 / $16.71bn, https://www.ig.com/en-ch/news-and-trade-ideas/goldman-sachs-stock-q3-2026-earnings-preview-261012), Zacks ($12.90 / $16.87bn, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:e051c3096094b:0-goldman-stock-before-q3-earnings-buy-now-or-wait-for-results/) and MarketBeat ($12.86 / $16.83bn, https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262211245-us-flcc-goldman-gs-tradingkey). Older late-September figures ($15.39 / $17.42bn, $15.18) are superseded. Segment bars are single-source: equities $4.68bn and IB fees $2.97bn (LSEG via IG), IB $2.76bn (Zacks). There is no FICC consensus found, so the FICC figure (~$4.1-4.3bn) is my own derivation and the findings resting on segment bars are capped small. GS gives no formal guide; the mid-quarter steers are from the Barclays conference on Sep 16.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 6.3M shares with 3.36 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (6.5M / 2.5 days at 06-30), about 2% of shares and not crowded (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/gs/short-interest/). No September settlement was found. The baseline 25d skew is -1.27 vol points, so calls are slightly richer, and put/call OI is 0.83; priced lean is balanced. The event-implied move is 3.84% (straddle 4.27%, ATM IV 47.5%); IG cites ±4.6%. The stock is -9.75% over 20 days, -22.6% off its July high of $1,153.99 and -12.2% in Q3, with the KBW bank index -13% from its August peak (Reuters via Globe and Mail, Oct 8).

findings.finding: The LSEG equities-trading consensus for Q3 is $4.68bn (IG, Oct 12). That is 37% below Q2's record $7.42bn and 12% below Q1's $5.33bn, although Q2 equities FINANCING alone was $3.26bn (Q1 $2.61bn, Q2'25 $1.71bn) and is balance-driven and sticky. Solomon said on Sep 16 that equities 'continues to be very strong'. Holding financing at $2.8-3.2bn plus intermediation near last year's Q3 level gives about $5.0-5.6bn, a $0.3-0.9bn beat on the line, worth roughly $0.5-1.5 of EPS against a $13 bar at about $1.7 EPS per $1bn of revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: record equities of $7.42bn against a ~$5bn estimate, with a 45% EPS beat, and the stock rose +9.0% (baseline 2026-07-14). Q3 2025 beat on trading but fell -2.04% on expenses and headcount.
findings.why_not_priced: The segment consensus models equities near Q3 2025 levels (+8% YoY) while the Q2 10-K-level line shows financing up 91% YoY. If the street had priced the financing run-rate, the equities consensus would be at or above $5bn and the EPS bar would not have been cut 17 times with no upgrades. The segment bar is single-source (IG/LSEG), so this is capped.
findings.independence: Q2 line items are from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000886982/000088698226000294/a2q26gsearningsresults.htm). Solomon's Sep 16 'very strong' is from https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/goldman-sachs-at-barclays-conference-solomon-touts-longterm-growth-93CH-4904307. Jefferies (Jun-Aug quarter) posted record equities revenue of $626m (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260928078906/en/Jefferies-Announces-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results).

findings.finding: FICC is the offsetting line. Solomon said on Sep 16 that FICC was 'a little bit softer', and Jefferies' fixed income for Jun-Aug fell 26% YoY to $176m. BofA guided trading flat and Citi mid-single-digit growth, and Q3 Treasuries had their worst quarter since 1994 (10y +87bp to 5.29%). The consensus revenue of $16.71bn less IB $2.97bn, equities $4.68bn, AWM ~$4.45bn and Platform ~$0.25bn implies FICC of about $4.1-4.3bn, close to Q2's $4.59bn and far above Q3 2025's $3.47bn. A FICC print of $3.6-3.9bn would be a $0.3-0.6bn shortfall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean single-line FICC reaction in the baseline. Q2 FICC rose 32% to $4.59bn inside a +9.0% day driven by equities.
findings.why_not_priced: The softness was public on Sep 16 and the EPS bar was cut afterwards, so part is priced. The residual is that the implied FICC consensus still sits near Q2 levels. That is an inference from a total, because no FICC consensus was found, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Jefferies FI -26% YoY (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2998277/jefferies-q3-ib-equities-offset-weak-asset-management-fixed-income). Peer guides from BofA, Citi and JPM come via Reuters/Globe and Mail (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-bank-third-quarter-earnings-preview/). The derived FICC bar uses the same IG document as finding 1.

findings.finding: LSEG league-table fees imply GS Q3 IB fees of about $2.45bn: 9M $8.2bn (Investment Executive, Oct 5) less H1 7.2% of $79.9bn, or about $5.75bn. Scaled by the reported/LSEG H1 ratio (6.235/5.75 = 1.08), that is about $2.65bn reported, against consensus of $2.76bn (Zacks) to $2.97bn (LSEG/IG). Industry fees fell 19% QoQ, BofA guided IB down more than 10% YoY citing Dealogic, and US IPO proceeds excluding SK hynix were only $6.2bn as deals were postponed in late September. GS keeps the #1 M&A adviser ranking and was a lead on SK hynix's $26.5bn ADR (~$260m fee pool split four-plus ways).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 IB fees rose 55% to $3.40bn inside the +9.0% day. No isolated IB reaction is visible in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus IB still sits at or above the league-table-implied figure. If the market had marked it, consensus would sit near $2.6bn. It is a proxy (league-table imputation, my subtraction across two LSEG releases), so it is small, and advisory is booked on completion, which the tables only approximate.

BofA's guide and Dealogic -10% via https://www.insiderfinance.io/news/bank-of-america-q3-investment-banking-fees-fall. Renaissance 3Q review (https://www.renaissancecapital.com/IPO-Center/News/121864/updated-renaissance-capitals-3q-2026-us-ipo-market-review). findings.finding: The EPS bar was cut sharply into the print, from $15.39 / $17.42bn (Sep 28-29 feeds) and $15.18 (Barchart, Sep 29) to $13.02 (LSEG), $12.90 (Zacks) and $12.86 (MarketBeat) by Oct 12. IG counts 17 downward revisions and no upgrades in 30 days, StarMine SmartEstimate is $12.80 and Zacks ESP is -5.9%, against a record of four straight beats averaging 20% (Q2: $20.98 vs $14.47).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are not always bought: Q2 2026 +9.0% on a 45% beat, Q4 2025 +4.63%, but Q1 2026 -1.87% and Q3 2025 -2.04% despite beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The cut itself is public and the stock is already 22.6% off its high, so the downside case is largely in the price. What is not obviously priced is that the bar now sits about 6% above Q3 2025 EPS of $12.25, on revenue expected up 10-11%. If the market were still braced for a miss, the skew would be put-bid; it is -1.27 (calls slightly richer).
findings.independence: Zacks (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:e051c3096094b:0-goldman-stock-before-q3-earnings-buy-now-or-wait-for-results/) and MarketBeat via TradingKey (https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262211245-us-flcc-goldman-gs-tradingkey) agree on ~$12.9. The earlier $15.39 is from https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/goldman-sachs-q3fy26-results-eps-seen-15-39-revenue-17-42-billion/52232381. This shares the IG document with finding 1, but rests on revisions rather than segment mix.

findings.finding: Company-guided headwinds for Q3, from Solomon on Sep 16: non-comp expenses 'more than $500 million higher sequentially' (Q2 non-comp ~$5.57bn), including a tax-efficient pull-forward of charitable giving; Investments 'much more muted' after Q2's $441m; provisions 'slightly higher' than Q3 2025's level (Q2 $102m) on idiosyncratic items. 'More than' is open-ended, and Q3's 10y +87bp could push private-equity marks negative rather than just muted.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: an EPS and revenue beat fell -2.04% on higher expenses and headcount (Seeking Alpha headline, Oct 14 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these items land inside what the company guided and preceded the estimate cuts. The residual is the open-ended 'more than $500m' and rate-driven marks.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs preview repeats the same guidance (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/goldman-sachs-q3-2026-earnings-gs-results-preview). Same underlying document as findings 1 and 2's Solomon quotes.

findings.finding: The forward pipeline the call will discuss. GS is a reported lead (with Morgan Stanley; FT says MS lead-left, GS stabilisation agent) on Anthropic's IPO, which Renaissance expects to headline 4Q26. Against that: late-September postponements (Oura, SB Energy), Solomon saying sponsor activity is slower than expected, and IB backlog having risen at end of Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GS gives no formal guide. Backlog commentary accompanied the +9.0% Q2 day; the Q3 2025 -2.04% came despite deal optimism.
findings.why_not_priced: The mandate is public; what is not priced is how much a Q4 mega-IPO and the backlog figure lift the Q4 IB run-rate after a soft Q3. With the stock 22% off its high on rates, a constructive backlog comment has room. Small, because it is widely reported.
findings.independence: Renaissance 3Q26 review on the Q4 pipeline and postponements (https://www.renaissancecapital.com/IPO-Center/News/121864/updated-renaissance-capitals-3q-2026-us-ipo-market-review). Reuters on IPO delays (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-us-bank-third-quarter-earnings-preview/).

baseline_tension: The skew (-1.27, calls slightly richer) and the deeply negative run-up (-9.75% 20d, -22.6% off high) do not fight a mild long. The negatives found (FICC, IB proxy, guided costs) are mostly what the market already sold the stock on, so the positive lean cuts against nothing strong; the risk is macro and the same-morning peer prints, which keeps p_up near 56.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): EPS bar confirmed by three agreeing sources, but the equities segment bar is single-source (IG/LSEG), so finding 1 was capped from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 5 (proxy/inference): the FICC bar is my derivation and the IB figure is league-table arithmetic, so FICC went from -0.8 to -0.5 and IB from -0.6 to -0.4; both stay filed.
Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): GS sold two of its last four beats (-1.87%, -2.04%), so the bar-cut finding went from +1.0 to +0.7 and p_up from 57 to 56.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): non-comp, investments and provisions are company-guided, so that finding moved toward 0 (-0.3 to -0.1).
Pipeline finding trimmed +0.3 to +0.2 as widely reported; abs_move_pct left at 4.5, above the 3.84 implied, since the hunters' sizes have run too small.
